instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each legislative agent to file a statement of expenditures with the updated registration statement.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(D)
instantiated_cells.justification: Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) must be filed by the last day of January, May, and September each year, and §101.73(D) ties expenditure statement timing to §101.72.
Section 101.72(B) sets filings due the last day of January, May, and September each year, i.e., three times per year.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(D)
instantiated_cells.justification: The statute specifies triannual filing with updated registration statements rather than a once-per-year spending report cadence.
Section 101.72(B) requires filings in January, May, and September only, not every quarter.
Section 101.72(B) sets three filing dates per year rather than two.
Section 101.72(B) does not require monthly expenditure statements, only filings by the last day of January, May, and September.
The only periodic filing cadence stated is triannual (January, May, September), with no other periodic schedule specified.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(B)(1); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(C)
instantiated_cells.justification: Legislative agents must report the total amount of expenditures made during the reporting period, and employers must report their total expenditures.

When expenditures are made for particular covered officials (or meal expenditures over $50), the statement must include the recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and legislative item/client information.
Section 101.73 requires disclosure of expenditure details tied to particular officials and certain meal thresholds, which is an itemized/detail format rather than only aggregate totals.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(B)(2)-(3); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.70(D)
instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires descriptions of expenditures and separately treats meals/food and certain function reporting, but it does not require expenditures to be categorized into standardized expense types.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.70(D)(1); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(B)(2)
instantiated_cells.justification: Expenditure is defined to include gifts and items such as food and beverages, entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and such expenditures to or for particular covered officials must be reported with details.
For reported expenditures, the statement must include the specific items of legislation, if any, for which the expenditures were made.
The updated registration statement (filed with the expenditure statement) must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated during the period.
The statute asks for the legislative item for which an expenditure was made but does not require aggregating or reporting expenditures per issue or bill as totals.
Section 101.73 requires totals and certain expenditure details but does not require reporting general issues addressed.
Initial registration includes a brief description of the type of legislation, but the expenditure statement requirements in §101.73 do not call for general subject-matter disclosure.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73; Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B)
instantiated_cells.justification: The statute requires listing specific bills/resolutions and reporting expenditures, but it does not require reporting the contacts made.

Section 101.73 expressly excludes 'the compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of expenditures for employer statements and does not otherwise require compensation reporting in the expenditure statement.

Because compensation paid to legislative agents is excluded from employer expenditure reporting and no compensation disclosure is required, there is no requirement to break compensation down by payer.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73; Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(A)(1)
instantiated_cells.justification: Lobbyist name/business address/occupation are required in the initial registration statement, but §101.73 does not require lobbyist contact information within the expenditure statement itself.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(B)(2)(e); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(A)(2)
instantiated_cells.justification: The expenditure statement must identify the client on whose behalf each expenditure was made, but it does not generally require listing all principal names beyond those tied to expenditures (and principal identity is primarily an initial registration element).

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73; Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(A)(2)
instantiated_cells.justification: Employer name and business address are required in registration statements, but the expenditure statement requirements in §101.73 do not call for principal/employer contact information as part of the spending report content.
Initial registration requires the agent’s occupation and a description of the type of legislation, but it does not require stating the principal's business nature in the expenditure statement.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(B)(2)(e)
instantiated_cells.justification: The law requires listing specific bills/resolutions and (if any) the items of legislation tied to expenditures, but it does not require disclosing a position (support/oppose) on legislation.
Employer reporting excludes office facility expenses, and the statute does not require disclosure of indirect/overhead costs as part of expenditures.

instantiated_cells.cited_section: Ohio Rev. Code § 101.72(B); Ohio Rev. Code § 101.73(A)
instantiated_cells.justification: Updated registration statements are required triannually to confirm continuing engagements and must be filed with a statement of expenditures, implying filing even if no reportable expenditures occurred during the period.
The expenditure definition covers expenditures made to or for specified public officers and certain staff, but it does not include household members of officials as covered recipients.

unscoreable_emissions.justification: Because no 'other' cadence is provided beyond the January/May/September schedule, there is nothing further to specify.
